Chain wear and customer communication:

When a bike chain is left dry, metal-on-metal friction increases, causing rapid wear. Without lubrication, the chain links grind against each other and the cassette, generating heat and metal shavings that accelerate corrosion and breakage. This not only shortens the chain's life but can also damage expensive components like derailleurs and cassettes.

Harbor Bikes employees, dry chains degrade rapidly due to oxidation and lack of lubrication. Without oil, metal-on-metal friction increases, causing premature wear on pins and rollers. This leads to stiff shifting, noisy rides, and eventual chain breakage.

When speaking to customers, explain that dry chains are the leading cause of unexpected maintenance costs. Emphasize that skipping a post-ride clean and lube saves nothing; instead, it accelerates failure, forcing them to buy a new chain sooner.
